pageCache.pageTitle: Music - Subjects - Epsom Primary and Nursery School
pageCache.text:
Music
At Epsom Primary and Nursery School, our aim is for children to develop an appreciation and enjoyment of music. Through our engaging curriculum, children will gain a firm understanding of what music is through listening, singing, playing, evaluating, analysing, and composing. We are committed to developing a curiosity for the subject, as well as an understanding and acceptance of all types of music. We aim to ensure that children understand the value and importance of music in the wider community by giving opportunities to perform to an audience we will see children grow in confidence as performers.
Our curriculum is centred on ‘Kapow’ in which the children develop a love of music, learn to sing and play instruments. They gain a sense of achievement through the opportunities to learn new songs and it is our aspiration that all children learn an instrument as part of a whole class percussion (percussion, recorder and glockenspiel). Their understanding of musical language and notation is built on as they progress through the school so that our children can read music, compose and improvise.
The enjoyment of music is at the forefront of our music teaching, as it enables our children to become more self-confident and develop a respect for and an appreciation of different music genres, which reflects our diverse community.
We encourage our pupils to be ambitious and approach musical learning with an inquiring and inquisitive mind. Our goal is to nurture a love for music through an enjoyable and inclusive learning environment where every child makes progress so that all children are ready for the next stage of their education.

Our Curriculum
History is taught in carefully planned units that progress through the school. Children begin by exploring their own lives and local history before moving on to study significant periods, people, and civilisations.
Examples from our curriculum include:
Reception – Peek into the Past

Pupils learn to use evidence to support their ideas and to make connections across time and place, preparing them for deeper historical study at secondary level.

pageCache.pageTitle: PE - Subjects - Epsom Primary and Nursery School
pageCache.text:
PE
Skills and Knowledge Progression with REAL PE
At Epsom Primary and Nursery School, REAL PE is used to provide a clear, engaging journey in physical education from EYFS to Year 6. Pupils develop fundamental movement skills, physical literacy and understanding of tactics, teamwork and fair play. They progress from mastering balance, coordination and agility to applying these skills across a variety of sports and challenges. REAL PE ensures every child experiences success, builds confidence and develops a lifelong love of being active, with assessment used to guide individual progress.
Innovation and Inclusion
REAL PE combines skill development with problem-solving and decision-making activities, encouraging pupils to think as well as move. Every child is included and challenged at their own level, building resilience, self-belief and leadership alongside physical competence.
Competitions and Team Sports
We are proud to represent our school in borough and district competitions, including athletics, football, netball and more. These events instil teamwork, sportsmanship, and competitive spirit, while our friendly matches ensure all pupils have the chance to take part.
Expert Coaching through NS Sport
Our partnership with NS Sport brings trained coaches into our lessons and clubs, offering specialist knowledge, tactical insight and inspiration. Their expertise raises the standard of our provision and motivates pupils to aim higher.
Linking REAL PE and NS Sport
REAL PE provides the essential building blocks of physical education—balance, coordination, agility, and decision-making—ensuring that all pupils have the skills and confidence to succeed. NS Sport then builds on this foundation, giving children the opportunity to apply these skills in a wide range of sporting contexts. This powerful combination allows pupils to transfer what they have learned in REAL PE into competitive games, team sports and enrichment clubs, deepening their understanding and enjoyment of physical activity.
Unlocking Sporting Excellence
Through REAL PE, expert coaching and regular competition, we continually nurture the sporting potential of every child. Alongside developing skills, confidence and determination, we place strong emphasis on the importance of healthy lifestyles and making positive choices around physical activity, nutrition and wellbeing. We aim for these habits to become part of each pupil’s life experience, inspiring them to remain active, healthy and engaged in sport long after they leave our school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Maths - Subjects - Epsom Primary and Nursery School
pageCache.text:
Maths
At Epsom Primary and Nursery School, we are passionate about enabling children to become confident, fluent mathematicians. Our inclusive and ambitious curriculum ensures that all pupils develop the knowledge, skills, and mindset to approach mathematical problems with curiosity and determination.
We follow a mastery approach built on the belief that every child is capable of understanding and succeeding in mathematics. Lessons are planned and delivered following the White Rose scheme of learning. Using small-step, carefully sequenced teaching, pupils progress fluidly through the curriculum, embedding their learning of the National Curriculum using concrete, pictorial and abstract representations of mathematical concepts.
A Mastery Approach to Teaching Mathematics
Our mastery model supports deep understanding and sustained progress. Each mathematical concept is explored through rich discussion, structured practice, and real-world application. Pupils are encouraged to reason, explain and justify their thinking using precise mathematical language.
By taking time to secure core understanding, we ensure that children build strong foundations—developing fluency, flexibility and confidence in their use of number, shape, space, and measure.
Mathematics with Purpose and Real-World Relevance
At Epsom, we nurture an appreciation for how mathematics shapes the world around us. Through zooming in and out, meaningful connections are built around nature, careers and daily life, children explore how maths is used in a range of real-world contexts. This includes hands-on opportunities and first-hand experiences that show how patterns and connections in maths relate to their lived experiences.
We foster collaborative learning and mathematical talk, encouraging children to discuss strategies, challenge assumptions and share solutions as active participants in their learning.
Inspiring Inquiry and Growth in Every Learner
We aim to nurture a love for mathematics by creating an enjoyable and inclusive environment where every child can thrive. Children are supported to be ambitious, to take risks in their learning and to approach each mathematical challenge with an inquisitive mind.
From Early Years to Year 6, our aim is to ensure that all children are well-prepared for the next stage of their education, confident in their mathematical ability and empowered to see themselves as successful mathematicians.

pageCache.pageTitle: EYFS Skills Progression - Subjects - Epsom Primary and Nursery School
pageCache.text:
EYFS Skills Progression
Our Early Years curriculum is carefully designed to support children in building knowledge and skills through a spiral approach, where learning is revisited, deepened and extended over time. Across all areas of provision, from water and sand play to construction, creative experiences and imaginative play, children begin by exploring materials through their senses and simple actions. They develop curiosity, begin to notice cause and effect, and use basic language to describe their experiences. These early interactions lay the foundations for communication, physical development and early mathematical understanding, as children repeatedly practise and refine their skills in meaningful contexts.
As children move into Nursery, these experiences are revisited with increasing complexity and purpose. They begin to experiment, predict outcomes and use a wider range of tools with greater control. Language develops from simple words to sentences, enabling children to describe, question and explain their thinking. They also begin to collaborate with others, create simple narratives and solve problems within their play. Across all areas, whether building structures, creating artwork or engaging in role play, children make connections between experiences and apply prior learning in new ways, demonstrating the strength of a curriculum that builds progressively over time.
By the time children reach Reception, they are able to plan, investigate and reflect on their learning with increasing independence and confidence. They use precise tools, apply subject-specific vocabulary and engage in sustained, collaborative play. Children solve practical problems, explain their reasoning and adapt their approaches, showing a secure understanding of key concepts such as measure, structure and cause and effect. This strong foundation ensures a smooth transition into Key Stage One, where children are well prepared to engage with more formal learning, bringing with them the curiosity, resilience and independence developed through our rich and carefully sequenced Early Years provision.

Examples from our curriculum include:
Through these units, children gain both technical skills and the ability to express ideas, feelings, and perspectives creatively.

pageCache.pageTitle: Computing - Subjects - Epsom Primary and Nursery School
pageCache.text:
Computing
Skills and Knowledge Progression with Purple Mash Our Computing curriculum uses Purple Mash to provide a clear pathway of skills and knowledge from EYFS to Year 6. Concepts are revisited and built upon – for example, moving from simple algorithms to complex programs or from basic image editing to creating multi-layered graphics. Pupils develop secure understanding of sequencing, selection, variables, data handling and online safety.
Innovation and Creative Application Purple Mash inspires pupils to become creators and problem-solvers. Projects often link with other subjects, giving real purpose to their learning. The platform’s flexibility allows for bespoke tasks that cater to different learning styles, encouraging experimentation, creativity and resilience through an iterative design process.
Physical Computing Physical computing is throughout our curriculum, with pupils using Purple Mash to program devices like micro:bits. They learn how to control LEDs, motors and sensors, applying their coding skills to practical challenges such as traffic light systems. This hands-on work makes programming concepts tangible, strengthens problem-solving skills and shows how technology impacts everyday life.
Preparing for a Changing Digital World Purple Mash equips children with the adaptability and critical thinking skills needed to thrive in an ever-changing digital landscape. By engaging with a broad range of tools, scenarios and problem-solving activities, pupils learn to respond to new technologies with curiosity, confidence and responsibility – ensuring they are not only ready for today’s challenges but also for the opportunities of the future.
Safeguarding Through Computing
Safeguarding is at the heart of our Computing curriculum. We use the Evolve Online Safety framework to teach children how to stay safe, respectful, and responsible when using technology. Lessons are carefully planned to cover topics such as online identity, privacy, cyberbullying, managing screen time, and recognising unsafe content or contact. By developing these skills from an early age, children learn how to make safe and informed choices online, while also understanding the importance of kindness, respect, and responsibility in the digital world.Computing Curriculum Overview 26 27Computing-Progression-Map-25-26Online-Safety-Progression-Map-KS1-25-26Online-Safety-Progression-Map-KS1-25-26Online-Safety-Progression-Map-KS2

pageCache.pageTitle: RE - Subjects - Epsom Primary and Nursery School
pageCache.text:
RE
Religious Education is an important part of our curriculum. It helps children to make sense of their own beliefs and values, while also developing respect and understanding for the diverse beliefs and practices of others.
Our Curriculum
RE is taught through an engaging and enquiry-based approach, where children explore big questions about life, meaning, and faith. Each year, pupils revisit key themes, gradually deepening their understanding as they progress through school.
Over the course of their time with us, children will explore questions such as:
By exploring these questions, pupils learn about Christianity and other major world religions, while also considering non-religious worldviews. This helps them develop critical thinking skills, empathy, and a balanced understanding of the role that faith and belief play in people’s lives.
What makes us special? (Reception)
Are all religions equal? (Year 4)
Who was Jesus really? (Year 5)
Government Guidance and Statutory Requirements
Although RE is not part of the National Curriculum, it is a statutory subject for all schools. Our curriculum follows national and local guidance, ensuring pupils receive a broad and balanced education that reflects Britain’s diverse society. In line with government expectations, we make sure that Christianity is taught in depth, while also introducing children to other principal religions and non-religious perspectives.
Parent Right to Withdraw from Religious Education
Parents and carers have the legal right to withdraw their child from all or part of Religious Education if they choose to do so. If you are considering this, we encourage you to speak with the Headteacher so we can discuss your wishes and any questions you may have. This helps us ensure that we fully understand your request and can make suitable arrangements for your child.
If you would like to request a withdrawal from RE, please contact the school office or speak directly with a member of the Senior Leadership Team.

pageCache.pageTitle: Phonics - Subjects - Epsom Primary and Nursery School
pageCache.text:
Phonics
Reading gives children the tools to become independent life-long learners. At Epsom Primary & Nursery School, we want to give children the best possible start to become fluent and confident readers and we do this by teaching the Read Write Inc (RWI) phonics scheme.
Phonics is taught from the very first day our Reception pupils enter the school. Children begin with the RWI Making a Strong Start programme, with whole class teaching during the first half term, before being assessed and grouped with the year 1 and 2 children. This allows children to work at their ability, without putting a limit on anyone’s learning.
In Reception and KS1, children begin their day with a 45 minute phonics lesson, taught by highly trained phonics staff. For those children who have completed the phonics programme their lesson focuses on comprehension and VIPER skills, preparing them for KS2.
In Nursery, during the Summer term, we begin to get our children ready for Reception by introducing them to the pictures and sounds associated with the RWI scheme.
For children who are identified as needing additional help, we have a dedicated RWI tutor who works with those pupils on a daily basis to help them keep up.
At the end of year 1, children take the Phonics Screening Check, a national assessment of their ability to decode 40 real and alien (made up) words.

Performance & Results
Understanding how we assess the progress and attainment of your children.
We are constantly gathering information about how your child is accessing their learning and making progress against the curriculum objectives. This then informs the class teacher’s planning and indicates where a child might need extra support, or extension, in a particular area.
Information is gathered in various ways
How do we share this information with you?
We are delighted to meet with you to discuss your child’s progress at any time. We send home reports at the end of every school year and hold Parent Consultation Meetings in the autumn and spring terms. If your child needs additional support, we will arrange a meeting to explain the interventions that your child will receive.
